scenarios.title: Peer routing contract
plannedActions: Run tracer app -- test services peer-signaling with the pinned published full Tracer runtime and isolated synthetic paid-team identities. The following describes its ordered relevant phases; content validation runs during the real signal TTL interval, as recorded in the complete catalog.
POST /v1/projects synthetic signaling team project
Connect three authenticated loopback project WebSockets
POST offer from A to B with forged sender fields
Wait for B signal and synchronize A and C sockets with ping watermarks
Read B inbox, C own inbox and C forged B inbox
Send binary JSON answer from B to A over WebSocket
Wait for A answer and synchronize B and C watermark barriers
Read A durable signaling inbox
POST exactly 50000 UTF-8 payload bytes as ICE
Read B inbox after initial offer cursor
Read complete B inbox as rejection baseline
POST signaling variant reject-large-payload
Read B inbox to verify rejected signal was not persisted
POST signaling variant reject-invalid-signal-type
Read B inbox to verify rejected signal was not persisted
POST signaling variant reject-nonobject-payload
Read B inbox to verify rejected signal was not persisted
POST signaling variant reject-invalid-recipient
Read B inbox to verify rejected signal was not persisted
POST signaling variant reject-expired-recipient
Read B inbox to verify rejected signal was not persisted
POST signaling variant reject-outsider-recipient
Read B inbox to verify rejected signal was not persisted
POST signaling variant reject-oversized-envelope
Read B inbox to verify rejected signal was not persisted
Send unsupported signalType over authenticated WebSocket
Read B inbox after rejected WebSocket signal
POST asset-request and asset-available signals from A to B
Read B inbox with explicit authenticated deviceId
GET B current authenticated session inventory before revocation
DELETE B secondary session through public auth route
Attempt revoked sender, revoked recipient and expired sender access
Read B pre-expiry inbox and wait past actual stored signal TTL
Read B inbox after actual 120-second expiry without clock manipulation
POST B logout then wait for its authenticated WebSocket close
Attempt B inbox access and A send to revoked B
Read final owner snapshot and isolated R2 object inventory
expectedOutcomes: HTTP 201 returns a synthetic project owned by the team owner.
Each authenticated socket receives hello for its own session and the empty project.
B receives exactly the A-authored offer through HTTP and WebSocket; sender fields cannot be forged; C own inbox and socket receive none; C reading B inbox returns 403 not_allowed.

Binary JSON WebSocket answer reaches A with exactly B authenticated device/user identity and payload in both live and durable envelopes; after B and C watermark barriers, B retains only its original offer and C has no signals.

Exactly 50000 UTF-8 payload bytes are accepted as ICE and returned exactly after the offer cursor; the complete B inbox is exactly the original offer plus accepted ICE and is saved as the rejection baseline.

The specific reject-large-payload input returns HTTP 413 signal_too_large; the complete intended inbox remains exactly the saved original offer and accepted ICE, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload.

The specific reject-invalid-signal-type input returns HTTP 400 invalid_signal; the complete intended inbox remains exactly the saved original offer and accepted ICE, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload.

The specific reject-nonobject-payload input returns HTTP 400 invalid_field; the complete intended inbox remains exactly the saved original offer and accepted ICE, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload.

The specific reject-invalid-recipient input returns HTTP 400 invalid_id; the complete intended inbox remains exactly the saved original offer and accepted ICE, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload.

The specific reject-expired-recipient input returns HTTP 404 peer_unavailable; the complete intended inbox remains exactly the saved original offer and accepted ICE, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload.

The specific reject-outsider-recipient input returns HTTP 404 not_found; the complete intended inbox remains exactly the saved original offer and accepted ICE, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload.

The specific reject-oversized-envelope input returns HTTP 413 body_too_large; the complete intended inbox remains exactly the saved original offer and accepted ICE, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload.

Unsupported signalType receives invalid_signal on the still-open authenticated sender socket; the entire B inbox, including IDs, timestamps, sender identity and payload, remains identical to the saved baseline.
Both supported asset notification types are accepted and returned with exact hash payloads in the intended explicit-device inbox.
Before revocation B sees its main and secondary live sessions, while its already-expired session is absent.
Public session revocation succeeds; revoked and already-expired senders receive session_expired and a revoked recipient receives peer_unavailable.

B inbox contains all four signals at an observation before the earliest stored at-plus-120000 deadline, and is empty at a later observation beyond the latest deadline; no continuous timing observation, clock or storage manipulation is claimed.
Public B logout closes its existing WebSocket with 4001; subsequent B inbox access returns session_expired and sending to B returns peer_unavailable.
Owner retains sequence seven and eleven items, R2 stays empty, outbound attempts and socket errors stay zero, and C has never received a signal.

associations.rationale: The public CLI journey exercises production HTTP/WebSocket routes and uses exact response and persisted-state assertions. The complete witness, fixture setup, production callers, guards and validators are included for independent audit.
associations.uncertainty: No race/interleaving claim, nonpremium cross-user denial, 100-row inbox pagination, physical asset transfer or production provider/network execution. TTL filtering is observed; expired-row physical deletion is not separately inspected.
proposedAssertions: Authenticated A offer is persisted only for B, reaches only B live socket, and ignores forged sender identity; C own inbox/socket stay empty and naming B deviceId fails with 403 not_allowed.

An exact 50000-byte UTF-8 payload succeeds and 50001 bytes fails signal_too_large; unsupported type, nonobject payload, malformed recipient and outer 65537-byte envelope fail their distinct guards. After each rejected HTTP or WebSocket signaling variant, the entire B inbox equals the saved original offer-plus-ICE baseline, including IDs, timestamps, sender identities and payload.

Expired and publicly revoked target sessions fail peer_unavailable; an outsider target fails project access. The binary-WebSocket answer has exactly B authenticated device/user identity and answer payload in both A live and durable envelopes. After B and C watermark barriers, B retains only its initial offer and C has no signals.

All four B signals are present at an observation before the earliest stored at-plus-120000 deadline, and B inbox is empty at an observation beyond the latest deadline. No continuous timing observation, clock manipulation or direct signal-store mutation is claimed.

associations.rationale: The public CLI journey exercises production HTTP/WebSocket routes and uses exact response and persisted-state assertions. The complete witness, fixture setup, production callers, guards and validators are included for independent audit.
associations.uncertainty: Bounded public-input contract, not exhaustive field/cartesian coverage. No native timing runtime, all word-order permutations, duplicate link IDs, every integer boundary or direct validation export is tested.
proposedAssertions: Fresh public commands accept independently specified NEL, BOM, combining-whitespace, emoji, empty and whitespace-only dialogue word arrays and exact snapshots preserve them; no native execution is inferred.

Exact identity, item-byte, finite-order, script-word, surrogate-boundary, unconfirmed-link, direction-word and authored-timing-source negatives return their specific errors without changing item state, head sequence or timing version.
A field-valid entry with an absent scene fails the separate ProjectRoom reference validation; field validation does not establish reference existence.

associations.uncertainty: No image bytes uploaded, image decoding, character-image-analysis or portrait geometry behavior, previous-version graph/cycle behavior, every timestamp/byte-count/ID boundary, or native UI execution is claimed.
proposedAssertions: One fresh public command accepts a coherent character, image metadata and anchored cue together with their referenced scene and entry; exact viewer snapshot fields match the submitted model, and viewer head sequence and timing version both equal one.

Whitespace/zero-width-only name, excessive aliases, unsafe filename, malformed digest, unsupported media, duplicate character tags, unpaired cue anchor and out-of-range cue offset fail with their specific errors and unchanged persisted state.
